I’ve turned a piece I posted last year on April Fools’ Day—with a few minor additions—into the first chapter. So, if you’re already familiar with it, feel free to skip this part.
-----
“Motoyasu, do you like me or —- more!?”
“Eh… um… oh, my phone’s ringing. I’ll be right back!”
I shook off —-chan—who had just told me she liked me—and ran away from the scene.
“Oh, Motoyasu!”
After all, it was true that, to me, both you and she were girls I liked equally… so I still couldn’t make up my mind. I’m supposed to talk with —-chan at my house tonight. I… just can’t bring myself to fully dislike my friend —. It’s not like — meant any harm when he teased —-chan. It was just that everyone around us jumped to conclusions, and it turned into underhanded bullying. Besides, isn’t it only natural for guys to talk to girls and go out with them?
I want everyone to get along. Bullying is just pathetic. That’s why I thought I’d confronted the bullying head-on and resolved it. So why did things turn out like this?
I… should I date my friend — or the sheltered rich girl —?
My friend — The rich girl — ←
But I also want to be with my friend —. I’m a junior in college, and I’ve dated various girls my whole life, but I realize this is the most difficult relationship I’ve ever been in. Why are the girls around me right now such a hassle? Yet I keep agonizing over the fact that I can’t seem to break free.
I’ve been enjoying the online game I’ve played since high school. It was actually a girl who introduced me to online gaming… and I ended up getting even more hooked on it than she did.
“Is it selfish to just want to have fun with everyone…?”
The bad thing about my friend — is that, even though she’s outgoing, she can be pushy. She shows up at my place unannounced, like a “ghost wife,” and cleans the house… but she ends up throwing my stuff away without asking. Then, when I went to —’s room, I found the things she said she’d thrown away, and when I asked her about it, she said she’d taken them because it seemed like a waste. On the other hand, the “princess” — shows up wherever I go with a frequency that’s way too high to be a coincidence… It’s not that she… forces her ideals on me, but I feel like I’m being watched. After finishing my classes that day, I went on a date with a girl I’d picked up recently before heading home.
And then… when I got back to my apartment, I heard a commotion coming from inside.
“Why are you at Motoyasu’s place?!”
“That’s exactly what I’m asking! —-san!”
I heard the sound of something shattering. I hurriedly opened the door. There, the two of them were in the middle of a physical fight.
“—is rich, so even if it’s not Motoyasu, there are plenty of other guys out there! Just give it up!”
“Motoyasu-san is the only one I love! He’s my prince! You could never make Motoyasu-san happy!”
“Don’t just assume things on your own!”
“Both of you, stop it!”
I stepped in between them and pulled them apart.
“Motoyasu!?”
“Motoyasu!”
Now that they’d finally noticed I was there, they seemed to calm down.
“Please tell —- and Motoyasu too! That I’m the one dating Motoyasu.”
“That’s not true! I’m the one dating Motoyasu!”
Oh, for heaven’s sake! Why are these two always fighting? I can’t even take them on a group date with a bunch of girls! They need to get along equally well with everyone!
“Since we’re on the subject, I’ll just say this: I’m not ready to date just one person yet. I don’t even want to think about that.”
“But…”
―― was speechless and took a few steps back. Her eyes widened as if she’d lost her temper—but in that split second, she grabbed a kitchen knife from the kitchen.
“What are you trying to do? Stop it!”
“It’s Motoyasu’s fault! He’s the one who made me like this! So—”
And with that, — dashed toward — with the kitchen knife. Determined not to let her do it, I braced myself to wrestle the knife away from her—but then I felt something pierce my side.
“Eh…”
When I turned around, —-san was holding the knife pressed against my side. Along with a sharp pain, an unbelievably red liquid began gushing from my body.
“Ahaha… You were on a date with a girl just a moment ago, weren’t you? I know. Rather than let —-san or anyone else take you, I’ll kill you and die myself. We’ll be together in heaven! Ahahahahahaha!”
—-san pulled the knife out with a squelching sound, like a broken doll.
“――, help――”
The wound felt hot, and I could feel my strength gradually draining away. On impulse, I called out to ―― for help. She snapped out of her stunned expression and rushed over to me. Then, with a thud, she plunged a kitchen knife into my chest.
“――”
I let out a scream that wouldn’t come out as a sound. I trembled uncontrollably, and blood gushed out in a torrent. I could feel the heat escaping from the depths of my body; even though I was burning up, I could feel myself growing colder and colder.
“I’m the one who’s going to be with Motoyasu in heaven! You can just die there on your own and go to hell!”
“You’re the one who’s going to hell!”
“Oh, really? I’m the one who killed Motoyasu, aren’t I?”
“He’s still alive! Motoyasu, please wait for me. I’ll put you out of your misery right now.”
And then—san aimed the knife at my throat—.
“I won’t let you get in my way! I’m the one who’s going to be with Motoyasu!”
“Do you really think you can beat me!?”
The two of them, blades in hand, continued their fight. I pressed my hand to my trembling chest and reached out into the void with blurred vision.
Am I—going to die? Why… why did it have to come to this? I… just wanted everyone to get along and have fun! I should have trusted all the girls equally… That’s right.
The one I know… wouldn’t do something like this—and she should be a kinder person, too. I just couldn’t bring myself to believe in the love they both felt for me. That’s why I should’ve told them properly. I have plenty of girlfriends. They all trust me, and I trust them. So I wanted to tell you both to trust each other and live happily.
I failed. I failed. I failed…
If—if there’s a next time, I’ll believe. Since all girls are angels, it’s my fault for not earning their trust.
Is this… what happened before I went to the world I thought was my “Emerald Online”…?
---
A long time has passed since then.
My name is Motoyasu Kitamura. I’m the Spear Hero who swore to protect Filo-tan and Filolial—the one destined to save the world. But—.
“Guhhhhhhh!?”
My HP dropped to zero, and a hole was torn right through my chest. I tried to look at my opponent’s face, but I couldn’t—my vision blurred… and I began to lose consciousness. Ah… this is the second time I’ve died, but it’s never a pleasant experience, no matter how many times it happens. Come to think of it, why was I so infatuated with that self-centered pig?
Come to think of it, the reason I came to this world was because that pig stabbed me. Back then, I… well, I had two girls I liked, but I kept agonizing over my indecisive attitude. Maybe my behavior annoyed her, because one of the girls I liked started viciously bullying the other, and when I stepped in to save her, the girl I’d saved wanted me all to herself… In the end, those two selfish girls came at me together with knives, trying to force a double suicide.
Which one stabbed me to death first? I’ve forgotten. That pig. I can’t even remember her face anymore.
But more importantly, Filo-tan.
That angel is amazing. She came to the world of a game I knew, and when I—naively—was trying to build a harem with casual relationships with women this time around, she dealt me a iron-fisted punishment to set me straight. The way she’d always come barreling at me and knock me aside whenever I was walking with a girl—that was all because she cared about me, wasn’t it!
In the end, neither my gaming knowledge nor my experience with women was much use, but meeting Filo-tan truly gave my life a new lease on life! That fucking Bitch tricked my Father, and I—who knew nothing—was manipulated into turning against him. Eventually, my Father raised Filo-tan… and I had my fated encounter.
A lot happened after that, too. Because of my mistake, I broke the seal on the Spirit Tortoise and threw the world into chaos. Unaware that I was being deceived, I chased after those running pigs, trying my best. And then… when I found out I was just a clown, Filo-tan encouraged me when I was feeling down!
“Cheer up!”
I’ll never forget the look on her face back then. I fought because I wanted to save the world for Filo-tan and Filolial. If that were the end of it… no matter what the outcome, I’d have no regrets.
Saying that… well, I think that’s… just a little bit of a lie. I want to see Filo-tan’s smile some more. I want to be with Filolial. I don’t want to die!
---
“Oh…”
When I looked ahead, I saw men in robes staring at us in astonishment.
“What is it?”
“Huh?”
I’m not sure whose voice it was, but it was probably Ren’s. Is this a dream? The scene before me is exactly the same as the one I saw when I was first summoned to this world. A magic circle has formed below us, and it looks as if we’ve just been summoned.
“Where am I?”
Ren is speaking to the castle’s wizard. This is a memory from that day… I see. It feels nostalgic. The day it all began.
“Oh, Heroes! Please save this world!”
“‘Huh?’”
My Father, Ren, and Itsuki all said it together. Right, right—I said the same thing along with them, didn’t I…? It’s a strangely realistic flashback.
Let’s check my stats just to be sure.
…They’re basically the same as before… Huh? They’re higher than I remembered. So, what’s this spear I’m holding?
Minute Hand of the Dragon Hourglass 0/300 LR Ability Unlocked… Equipment Bonus: Ability “Time Reversal” Special Effect: Branching Worlds
What’s with this spear? I open the Weapon Book to check. Most of the spears listed are ones I recognize. But there are some I don’t… though it doesn’t look like I can switch them out.
What’s going on? The level is higher than I remember—what’s happening here? And what’s this “Time Reversal” equipment bonus for this spear, anyway? I learned from my Father that my knowledge of the game isn’t exactly helpful… Huh?　Did I really learn that? I can’t quite remember.
Um… I can remember up to the point where Filo-tan encouraged me, but after that, it’s as if a fog has settled over my memory—I can’t recall a thing. But there’s one thing I do remember.
This overflowing love I have for Filo-tan and Filolial!
I don’t know if this is a dream or if I’ve traveled back in time thanks to some lucky ability, but there’s only one thing I can do: fight for the world!
“Hm?”
Ren and Itsuki are looking at me. And then…
“Just how much of our intentions are you going to take into account?”
“Depending on what you say, we might end up becoming enemies of the world. Please be prepared for that.”
Ren and Itsuki both repeated the exact words I had said. My Father looks like he’s just lost a bet.
“Well, first of all, I’d like you to have an audience with the king. We’ll discuss your reward at that time.”
---
The head wizard of the castle had the door opened and was about to show us in.
“…I guess I have no choice.”
“Exactly.”
“Come on, let’s go.”
I held out my hand to my Father.
“Ah, ah.”
Somehow, Father’s face looked brighter—or rather, more childlike—than I remembered. Innocent, that’s the feeling. If I asked him to give me his daughter right now, would he? …Wait a minute. If I really did travel back in time, my Father hasn’t even raised Filo-tan yet, has he!? Just as I was thinking this, we were led into the throne room. Oh, there’s that Trash.
“Hmm, so these are the ancient heroes, are they?”
He’s staring at us intently. What an outrageous old fogey. I can’t even imagine how much my Father must have suffered at the hands of this guy…
“I am the king of this realm, Aultcray Melromarc the 32nd. Lift your heads, heroes.”
Ah, come to think of it, that was his name. I’d completely forgotten. What was I thinking at that moment? I remember thinking something like “Yay!” about traveling to another world, and getting even more hyped once I learned about the system. Then I was supposed to explain the “Wave,” right? Actually, the Wave is… Huh? I can’t remember. That’s strange—I distinctly remember it being a very important issue. Is this a side effect of time travel? Probably—no doubt about it. Memories of my dates with Filo-tan are fading in places!?
“True, I don’t really have any obligation to help them. It’d be a real pain to work for free only to be told ‘goodbye’ once peace is restored. Actually, I want to ask if there’s a way to get back—what’s the deal with that?”
“Grr…”
Father’s voice snapped me back to reality. I’d been lost in thought and hadn’t been listening. This isn’t the time for that anyway, and since I do remember this part, I should be fine—I hope. More importantly, the memories of Filo-tan that I was supposed to take to my grave have vanished. How can I remember them? Hmm? Come to think of it, instead of trying to remember, I should just create new memories. I’m a genius.
“Hey…”
My father gave me a light nudge with his elbow.
“Huh? What?”
“Oh, just introducing yourself.”
“Ah, my name is Motoyasu Kitamura, and I’m twenty…”
How old was I again? Wait, physically speaking, am I twenty-one now?
“Twenty?”
“No, twenty-one.”
“And your occupation?”
“I’m The Love Hunter.”
“Huh?”
I’ve already cast aside that boring title of “Spear Hero” because I’m fighting to win Filo-tan’s heart.
“He’s probably unemployed,”
Itsuki added. Well, say whatever you want. My days with Filo-tan, fueled by my love, can’t be defined by a job.
“Hmm… Ren, Motoyasu, and Itsuki, huh?”
“Don’t you dare forget my name, Father!!!!!!!”
“Huh!?”
Of all things, to forget my father’s name! Come to think of it, this Trash was the father of that pig, wasn’t he! I’ll teach him a lesson.
“Father!?”
My father cried out in surprise. Damn it. Saying something like that in this situation will just make him suspicious. First impressions are everything. I need to make sure he has a good impression of me—otherwise, he won’t let Filo-tan marry me.
“Ah, sorry. You look exactly like my special someone’s Father, so I just blurted it out.”
“H-huh… Do I really look that old?”
“No, no—you look almost exactly the same, so you’re young.”
“How old is the girl you like!?”
“I think…”
How old was she again? I’m totally vague on Filo-tan’s age…
“She hasn’t been born yet.”
“…You’re something else, aren’t you?”
“Is that so? Father.”
“Are you going to call me that? Could you please stop, if possible?”
“Heroes, please keep your private conversations to a minimum.”
A rather inconspicuous minister calls us out. Oh right, this Trash keeps forgetting my Father’s name.
“Well, let’s get back to the main topic. Your Father’s—”
“Um, Kitamura-kun. Please stop calling him ‘Father.’”
“Understood. I’d like you to correct your intentional omission of Naofumi-kun’s name.”
“‘Intentional?’”
“Yeah, this Trash thinks this country treats the Shield Hero—”
“Waaaaaaah! I’m so sorry. It was my fault, Spear Hero. Please calm your anger.”
Hmm… It seems even Trash is showing some remorse. The authority of the Four Holy Heroes is still quite potent.
“Calling the King ‘Trash’? Who do you think you are?”
Ren asks me warily. Hmm? Did I say something strange? I thought this guy’s name was Trash… …Ah, come to think of it, he did have a proper name to begin with.
“I’m The Love Hunter.”
“……”
I feel like Ren’s gaze just turned cold. Did I say something weird?
“Hmm… I’ve gone off on a tangent, but everyone, please check your stats and take an objective look at yourselves.”
“Huh?”
Why bring that up now…? I already checked my stats. They’re exactly the same. It’s like a ‘New Game Plus’! This is way too easy. The first wave is so weak there’s nothing to do.
“Um, how do we check them?”
“What’s wrong with you guys? Didn’t you notice this right after arriving in this world?”
Ren, looking like the go-to expert, starts to give a run-of-the-mill explanation. Alright, this is my chance to impress my Father!
“Wha—”
“Don’t you see an icon somewhere in the corner of your vision? Try focusing your attention on it.”
“Huh?”
Ren’s totally dumbfounded that I beat him to it. What a total goofball.
“Level 1, huh… That’s a little worrisome.”
“I mean, what even is this?”
“It doesn’t exist in the Hero’s world, does it? This is Status Magic—something anyone in this world can use.”
“Is that so?”
I guess even my father had a time like this. The Father I know has a sharp gaze, a sharp tongue, and a short fuse, but it’s nice that he seems open to reason.
“So, what are we supposed to do? You’re right—this level is a bit worrying.”
“Hmm. We’d like you, the Heroes, to set out on an adventure, hone your skills, and strengthen your Legendary Weapons.”
“Strengthen them? Aren’t the weapons we’re holding already strong to begin with?”
“Yes. According to legend, summoned heroes are meant to nurture and strengthen the Legendary Weapons they possess.”
When I stayed silent, my Father fell into a troubled silence before speaking up.
“Even if you call it a Legendary Weapon, I’ve got a shield. Wouldn’t it be better to use a sword?”
Ah, he doesn’t know.
“It doesn’t seem to work that way. The thing is, you can’t equip any other weapon while you’re wielding this Legendary Weapon.”
“Whoa!? Is that really true?”
“That’s right, so… Naofumi, you’d better rely on your party members.”
“Does that mean the four of us are forming a party?”
“That won’t work either.”
“Huh?”
“The Hero’s weapon will repel them, so they won’t gain any EXP. You can share the materials used to level up the weapon, though.”
“Please wait a moment—”
“Hm?”
Interrupted by me, the Minister fell silent.
“You seem strangely well-informed, Motoyasu-san.”
Itsuki looked at me with a puzzled expression.
“Ah, I’m from the future.”
“…I see.”
He believed me without a second thought. Everyone’s so kind these days.
“So, what were we talking about?”
He asked the Minister. Didn’t he hear what I said? It seems he didn’t believe me.
“Well, what the Spear Hero said is more or less correct. Apparently, having two Heroes together hinders their growth.”
My Father seems to be browsing the system. He’s probably reading the help section.
“It seems to be true… In that case, should I recruit some companions?”
“I’ll take care of finding you some companions. After all, the sun is already setting. Hero, you should rest well tonight and set out tomorrow. I’ll gather some promising candidates who might join you by then.”
Hmm… I can see a scheme brewing. I absolutely have to be careful.
“Thank you.”
“Thanks.”
“To the Shield Hero—”
“I know! I’ll gather them! I’ll definitely gather people who’ll join us!”
That Trash tells me to shut up. Well, I guess it’ll be okay?
---
In the guest room’s luxurious bed, everyone except me was staring intently at their weapons while listening to the explanation. It’s pretty ironic that all these guys, whose hearts are racing with anticipation… are going to end up going through such hell. Father will be next pretty soon.
“Hey, this is kind of like a video game, isn’t it?”
“It does seem like a game, but it’s a little different—”
“This world is the world of a console game.”
“That’s not right. It’s a VRMMO.”
“Huh? VRMMO—as in Virtual Reality MMO? Isn’t that something from the future?”
“What the—!? What are you even talking about?”
“Hold on, hold on.”
I stepped in to cut off everyone’s discussion. We should’ve already reached a conclusion.
“Rin, Itsuki, and Naofumi. Listen carefully.”
“W-what is it?”
“Everyone here comes from completely different worlds. Even within Japan, they’re totally different. Just keep that in mind.”
“I-is that so?”
“Yeah, I’m pretty sure Itsuki’s world is…”
Huh? There was supposed to be something about Itsuki’s world that was different from both the world I know and my Father’s world. Elements that Itsuki himself isn’t aware of—which makes sense, of course—but seem strange to us…
“My world is… what?”
“I forgot.”
“Wait, you’ve been strangely detailed about this since a little while ago—what’s going on?”
“I told you, didn’t I? I’m from the future.”
“Ah, yeah, yeah.”
I got swept along by Ren.
“Still, there’s some truth to what this self-proclaimed time traveler says. Let’s try to piece the information together.”
My Father and the others ignored what I said and started drawing their own conclusions on their own. Hmm… They don’t believe me? This is disheartening. So they don’t believe in knowledge from the future, huh? I just got transported to another world—you’d think they’d at least believe in supernatural phenomena like that. But I’ll let my Father know anyway.
“I’ll stay up all night to teach Naofumi-kun, who doesn’t know anything.”
“Ah, thank you… You’re so kind, Motoyasu Kitamura.”
“You’re welcome, you’re welcome. Please just call me Motoyasu. In return, I’ll call Naofumi-kun ‘Father.’”
“Please, stop it!”
He rejected me with a look of utter disgust. Hmm, does that reaction mean I messed up?
“Trusting in a hero’s weapon is part of what makes it powerful. You can get stronger by learning how I, Ren, and Itsuki have enhanced ourselves. Ren and Itsuki might say their classes have weak shields, but don’t worry—they’re incredibly strong. They have stats on par with ours.”
That’s right. Back then, everyone’s hearts were scattered, so we ended up putting a burden on my Father, but now we should be able to start over.
“Ren and Itsuki, listen to me. The knowledge I have might be different from what you all know. But by believing, the way to strengthen yourselves will become clear.”
“Ugh. Fine.”
“…Hmph.”
Their reactions are lukewarm. It seems they don’t trust me… How can I get them to believe me?
“Well, I guess I’ll go ahead and ask him.”
Just as I’d expect from my Father. No matter what, he’s always hungry for power. Just as I was about to start explaining…
“Hero, dinner is ready.”
We were called to dinner.
“Then I’ll explain after we eat.”
“Thank you.”
And so, I ended up staying up all night teaching my Father how to enhance this weapon.
---
As I was patiently explaining the enhancement method to my Father, he gradually drifted off to sleep. It seemed the sudden lecture had worn him out. After checking on Ren and Itsuki, who were already asleep, and making sure my Father was in bed, I set out for a nighttime stroll. The interior of the castle was just as I remembered… However, the view outside was slightly different.
The Spirit Tortoise Mountain was gone. This dreamlike moment felt far too long to be just a fleeting memory. Maybe… I really had traveled back in time.
If I’m here… maybe Filo-tan will agree to marry me! As I walked through the garden thinking that, I caught a whiff of Filolial! I followed the scent and discovered a shed where Filolials were kept.
“Gua!”
“Gua!”
It was late at night, so the Filolials seemed to be fast asleep. Ah, that scent. I can’t stand it anymore. Come to think of it, I haven’t smelled a Filolial in over half a day since arriving in this world. I’m starting to get withdrawal symptoms.
“Good evening~”
“Gua!?”
When I entered the Filolial enclosure to say hello, the Filolials woke up, startled. Then they looked at me with a somewhat wary expression.
“D-don’t be wary, Filolial-sama.”
“Gua?”
They aren’t making that “kue” sound… It seems they miss Filo-tan. But they’re Filolial-samas! I absolutely must replenish my Filolial fix.
“Here, here—I shall present you with your meal.”
I help myself to some dried meat from a nearby warehouse and present it to the Filolial-samas. Curious about the offering, they scramble to devour the dried meat I’ve brought.
“In return, may I give you all a good cuddle?”
They don’t seem to have been raised smart enough to understand human speech, but the Filolial-sama appear to be in a good mood.
“‘Gua!’”
“What a blessed joy.”
I touched the Filolial-sama, ran a comb through their feathers to my heart’s content, and breathed in their scent—and before I knew it, I was fast asleep alongside them.
---
“Doesn’t Kitamura-kun smell a little funny?”
The next morning, having woken up feeling refreshed, I met up with everyone.
“How rude to call it a ‘smell’—it’s the noble scent of Filolial-sama.”
“Filolial-sama?”
“Filolial-sama are Filolial-sama.”
“That’s not an explanation.”
“They are bird-like monsters that pull carriages,”
the minister acting as our guide added.
“Ah… those, right?”
My father-in-law nodded, as if he understood. After waiting a while, we were summoned.
“The Hero has arrived.”
When we reached the throne room, the pig and a group of men were waiting. About a dozen of them in total. For the sake of appearances, we all bowed our heads to Trash. I resented having to bow to Trash. But since Ren, Itsuki, and my Father were doing it, I had no choice but to follow suit.
“Regarding yesterday’s matter, I put out a call for those who wish to journey alongside the Hero. It seems you all have a Hero you’d like to accompany.”
I’m pretty sure the old me was hoping a girl would come to me. I don’t really care about that now. If anything, I’m worried about my Father. I’ve left him all alone.
“Now then, future heroes. Set out on your journey with the Hero you wish to serve.”
Ren, Itsuki, and my father look surprised. Oh, right—I was the one who was supposed to be chosen. The people who want to be my companions are gathering around me.
Ren: four. Itsuki: three. Me: three. My father: two.
“I’m one short here…”
My father voices his dissatisfaction. I’d think that’s a big improvement from the zero I had before, though.
“Ren, spare one for him.”
As soon as he says that, Ren’s companion? hides behind Ren like a shield. As for me, I’m stuck with nothing but pigs—it’s a real pain. Actually, there are so many pigs it’s gross enough to make me want to throw up.
“Oink!”
“Oink-oink-oink-oink-oink!”
I can’t make heads or tails of what they’re saying. Ugh… Father’s group has two pigs, too. There are just too many pigs—it’s a real problem.
“Naofumi-kun, if you don’t mind, I’ll give you three of mine.”
“Really!? But Kitamura-kun, if you do that, won’t you end up alone…?”
Just as you’d expect from the modest Father of Filo-tan. To think he’s even considering me…
“Hero, please refrain from swapping companions without permission.”
“Mmm…”
I’d really rather not go on an adventure with pigs.
“Now, here is your starting allowance. Heroes, be sure to accept this.”
Four pouches of gold were distributed in front of us. I heard a heavy, jingling sound. I’m pretty sure it was 600 silver coins.
I’m worried about the red pig standing next to my Father. Maybe it’s just my imagination, but I have a bad feeling about this.
“Each hero will receive 600 silver coins. Use them to gear up and set out on your journey!”
“‘Yes, sir!’”
I heard a “Oink!” sound! Hey, you!
---
So, after receiving the silver coins and preparing to set out on our journey, I tried to speak to my Father, but the pig cut me off.
“Oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink.”
“Oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink.”
I have absolutely no idea what it’s saying. Anyway, I need to step in and help my Father out…
“Oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink”
“Get out of the way! Move it!”
I tried to push the pig aside to get closer to my Father, but the pig kept getting in the way. What a persistent pig. They’re not well-trained here in this country.
“Oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink!”
“Um… Spear Hero? Isn’t that attitude a bit much toward your companion?”
A castle soldier called me out.
“I don’t care. He’s fired on the spot.”
“Oink-oink-oink-oink-oink-oink!?”

I’ve got to get there in time!

“It’s been a while since I’ve used this.”
I focused my consciousness on the spear and locked onto the enemies with a skill that has high accuracy but lacks power.

I threw the glowing spear with all my might. Aiming Lancer. Back when this was just a game, it was a skill that granted a high accuracy bonus. Its damage was mediocre—only slightly stronger than the Air Strike Javelin. url: https://ncode.syosetu.com/n3009bk/460
translator: deepl_quality_optimized
+++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
I’ll use the portal to return to Melromarc Castle, set Yuki-chan and the others’ eggs in the incubator… and register their monster crests.
“Kou’s egg too…”
So, after finishing Kou’s registration, I’ll take a look at Sakura-chan’s egg. …Hmm. Sakura-chan is Filolial-sama, who was closest to my Father. After all, he had originally entrusted her with guarding him. I have a vivid memory of how close she was to my Father.
I, Motoyasu, know this. My Father had become a bit reserved because everyone had been helping him level up. If Sakura-chan were here to grow alongside him and protect him, he might be able to let his guard down a little more.
Yeah. Even though she’ll fall a little behind Yuki-chan and the others, let’s keep Sakura-chan around without contracting her as Father’s personal Filolial-sama. It’s a bit of a hassle, but it might be good for Father to grow alongside Sakura-chan. So, let’s have Father register Sakura-chan.
“‘Boo-boo!’”
Hm? I turned around at the sound of some unpleasant squealing, and a pig was pointing at me, squealing as it approached. That completely ruined the happy mood I was in just a moment ago. Stay away, you filthy creature.
As I thought that and looked around, I noticed the sun was already setting quite low. It seems it’s about time I found a place to stay and get some rest. Completely ignoring the pigs, I stashed the egg away and headed for the inn where I’d stayed on the first day.
Later, as I was waiting at my usual nighttime tavern, the Crimson Swine showed up, so after nodding along half-heartedly, I hurled some insults at him.
“Oink! Oink-oink-oink-oink-oink!”
That oinking is so noisy. Should I just wipe him out right here and now?
I do think that, but I can easily imagine that if I were to eliminate the Crimson Swine here, it would lead to a future I know nothing about. He’s a piece of Trash, after all. I can guarantee he’ll mock me to my Father—who’s searching for the Crimson Swine after he went missing—calling me a foolish hero who let his comrades escape.
If I’m not careful, he might even make up a story about where I took his daughter and pin a false charge on me. I’ll stick to what my Father said last time. I’ll make a special exception and hold back from taking out the Crimson Swine right now.
“Oink, oink!”
“You’re being persistent. No matter how long you keep squealing, I won’t be fooled by you. You thieving pig!”
“Know this: the only reason you’re still alive is because of my Father’s mercy!” Oink, oink—squealing in response to my insults and seething with rage, Crimson Swine fled the scene. He’s heading straight for Itsuki, I suppose.
Seriously… isn’t there some way to eliminate the Crimson Swine without interfering with the future? It’s frustrating, isn’t it? According to my Father, the Crimson Swine is a tough one to get rid of. If we can avoid war, it might be possible to eliminate him. That’s around the time the Crimson Swine got heavily involved in the commotion, wasn’t it? After that, according to my Father, he curried favor with Ren and Itsuki, and then joined forces with Smoked Meat and the remnants of the Three Heroes Church to launch a revolutionary movement.
So that means… it was after the battle against the Pope. The immediate challenge is how to gain Ren and Itsuki’s trust. Even now, when I think back on the aftermath of that battle, it brings back bitter memories. I charged in thinking I could defeat the Spirit Tortoise, only to let those pigs escape and end up chasing after them for ages.
Chasing after pigs who can’t think of anything but themselves is a waste of time. My spirit was worn down, and… I was encouraged by Filo-tan. After that, I felt a sense of happiness… I awakened to true love.
In that sense, the Crimson Swine was extremely helpful, so let’s execute him painlessly as an act of mercy. We must figure out a way to eliminate the Crimson Swine early on and find a stable foundation free of problems. To put my knowledge of the future to good use… and to put my Father’s words into practice, I must learn the things I was previously unaware of.
If we enter the next loop, what I need to do is find out where my Father, Ren, and Itsuki are within the first few days after I’m summoned. It seems the companions we were introduced to were tasked with subtly keeping my Father and the other heroes at a distance—even going so far as to frame him with false accusations—to prevent them from getting along. During the first loop after the cycle restarted, every attempt I made to get close to my Father was thwarted, but when I acted cool and kept my distance, he simply followed along without incident.
As for the inn, it seems they went ahead and prepared a room for us to stay in on their own. It’s true that they’re interfering to prevent the heroes from coordinating with each other. Father’s specialty is doing things that annoy his opponents—that’s his way of winning a fight. To secure a future where the heroes get along, I’ll be gathering information this time around.
Of course, I have no intention of wasting this loop. After all, I haven’t given up on my dream of finding Filo-tan and becoming her master. There are plenty of ways to make money without making a big move. Well, putting that into action will have to wait a little longer.
Fortunately, since I’d purchased the Filolial-sama eggs from that monster merchant Motoyasu, I can generally tell who’s going to hatch just by the smell and texture. Well, even though the species were different, there weren’t any of Kuu’s eggs during the last loop, so I suppose it depends on the season.
In that case, I’ll just have to visit frequently and keep looking for eggs from Filolial-sama I haven’t encountered before. After all, there weren’t any of Kuro-chan’s eggs during the last loop either, so timing really is crucial.
“Well then… I suppose I’ll get some sleep.”
Back at the inn, I went to bed hugging Yuki-chan and the others’ eggs.
---
The next morning. As expected, since I’d berated the Crimson Swine, I didn’t get a summons. So, I headed to the castle earlier than I did the time before last. As I approached the castle, the soldiers greeted me with anxious expressions.
“What brings you here so early in the morning?”
“Am I not allowed to come to the castle just for the sake of it?”
“We’re a bit swamped right now, so please come back after the sun has fully risen.”
Just then, Ren and the others arrived in a carriage from behind, looking rather displeased.
“Oh? Isn’t that Motoyasu? Were you summoned too?”
“…Yes, I was.”
It’s better to go along with Ren’s conversation here so I can get in without resorting to force. When I looked at the soldier blocking the path, he turned pale upon realizing he couldn’t possibly ignore me and let Ren into the castle.
“What’s the matter?”
“…Please. Go ahead, Sword Hero.”
“What about Motoyasu? He was summoned just like me, wasn’t he?”
“That’s right, isn’t it? Are you not going to let me in?”
“……”
The soldiers are exchanging confused glances. With that kind of attitude, Ren’s going to get suspicious, you know?
“What’s going on? Or is there some reason you’re only calling me and not Motoyasu?”
“No… I understand. Please come this way, Spear Hero.”
“Then I’ll be on my way.”
This is a win. If I time my arrival to coincide with Ren and the others, I won’t have to force my way in.
“Motoyasu, where are your companions?”
“They’re sleeping at the inn. They were sleeping so soundly that I didn’t want to wake them, so I came alone.”
“I see…”
“Where was Ren staying?”
“Me? I was resting in the village two stops past the castle town when I got summoned.”
“I see… Which village, exactly?”
I picture the map of Melromarc in my mind. “Two stops past the castle town” narrows it down quite a bit. Within that range, there are only two or three villages I could reach in a single day.
“That would be—”
It seems Ren had been heading southeast from the castle town. Come to think of it… I just remembered how we discussed things back in the first world to avoid overlapping hunting grounds. I see—I’d better keep that in mind.
Well, since Itsuki has been taken over by the Crimson Swine, it looks like I’ll have to wait a little longer to get any information out of him. As I made my way through the castle and entered the Throne Room, the Crimson Swine, Itsuki, and Trash were waiting there.
“Calling me out this early the very next morning after telling me to set out on my journey… What’s with this sudden summons?”
As soon as they realized I was standing next to Ren, Trash and Itsuki looked distinctly displeased. However, it seemed they prioritized explaining the situation. The Crimson Swine, oozing filth from its eyes and grunting, was speaking to Ren.
This… I’m starting to remember now. If I recall correctly, in the first world, I was standing right where Itsuki is now. Just as I was about to be raped by my Father, the Crimson Swine came running to the inn where I was staying and clung to me, squealing.
After that, the Crimson Swine suggested we report it to the castle, so we went there, where Trash put on a serious act, taking the situation very seriously, and called for Itsuki and Ren. Then the Crimson Swine started wailing things like, “I was almost raped by the Shield Hero. I was so scared…” and “Please, save me from that rapist!” and so on. Her acting was so convincing that both Ren and Itsuki were convinced I was unforgivable.
The Crimson Swine is getting uncomfortably close to Ren, oozing filth while grunting and making a racket. Then the Crimson Swine points at me and squeals.
“Motoyasu, is it true that you called this child a pig?”
“A pig is a pig. Slandering others and covering up misdeeds—if that isn’t a pig, then what is?”
“Covering up misdeeds?”
“Oink, oink.”
When Ren furrowed his brow, the Crimson Swine stepped between me and Ren and tried to shove me aside. But maybe it doesn’t understand how strong I am—it didn’t budge an inch. Hey, you’re supposed to speak human language properly.
You’re probably just spouting some lie anyway. My ears are about to rot from listening to this. I casually keep standing next to Ren. Itsuki has been glaring at me the whole time.
“Is there something you want to say?”
“I’ve been thinking about this since yesterday—what’s with calling a woman a pig?! She’s a human being, you know.”
“Hahaha, you must be joking.”
“What’s so funny?!”
As always, Itsuki’s such a clown. Wearing stolen chainmail and acting all righteous—that’s beyond ridiculous.
“If you really think that, you’d better find out where that chainmail was sold.”

“This is something I received from Myne.”
“That’s exactly why I’m saying it’s stolen goods!”
“Don’t just make things up. Do you have any proof?!”
“Weapons and armor in this country have inscriptions and serial numbers. Where and by whom that chainmail was purchased—”
“Oink! Oink-oink!”
Just as I was about to present my evidence, the Crimson Swine stepped in and interrupted me in a loud voice.
“Don’t interrupt, Crimson Swine!”
I shoved him aside with a thud and said to Itsuki,
“It’s set up so we can tell.”
“…Is that really true?”
Itsuki asked Trash and Crimson Swine. Then Trash stroked his chin just once.
“Well then, Lord Kawasumi, might we see that chainmail? Let’s cross-check it.”
A soldier brought a tray over to Itsuki. Reluctantly, Itsuki took off his chainmail and placed it on the tray. After that… the soldier went over to Trash once and began the verification.
“It seems, according to our records, this chainmail was in our castle’s warehouse!”
That scum! It looks like he fabricated the records! It seems he’s got just enough wits to come up with something like that.
“That doesn’t change the fact that you stole it from the castle.”
“Oink! Oink-oink!”
At that moment, the Crimson Swine sprang to his feet and, walking with a foolish gait that pretended to be elegant, started making a commotion.
“Oink! Oink-oink-oink-oink…”
“I see… So Myne was a princess? In that case, the items from the castle certainly belong to her.”
Ugh… He fabricated evidence and revealed his own identity to claim he wasn’t a thief. It seems Itsuki has completely fallen for the Crimson Swine and that Trash’s delusional ramblings. However… Ren looks as though he has his doubts about this exchange.
“…There are many points that don’t add up, but it’s none of my business. It’s too early to judge which side is right.”
That said, Ren probably won’t take Father’s side here.
“That’s exactly it, Motoyasu-san! She isn’t a pig, nor is she evil. Didn’t she simply try to give you the castle’s belongings out of goodwill? Your response to that is absolutely unforgivable.”
“No matter what you say, a pig is a pig. To begin with, I can’t trust the verification done by the pig’s parents.”
“What did you say?!”
“The fact that she confessed to being a princess makes it even worse. After all, it’s easy for a princess to tamper with evidence.”
It happens all the time, doesn’t it? Stories where the children of the wealthy commit crimes, and their parents use their power to cover it up. That’s exactly what’s happening here. Besides, I’ve heard that under modern law, family testimony carries little weight as evidence. Well, I don’t know if that applies in this world, though.
“…Motoyasu does have a point.”
“Renn-san, whose side are you on?!”
“Hmph, I’m not on either side. But Motoyasu’s argument does hold some merit. If he were just a common adventurer, I might trust the king’s words, but when it comes to his daughter, that’s a different story. Besides, if the kingdom and the princess were really framing Naofumi, the evidence from earlier would have been tampered with by now.”
As Ren replied, Trash interjected.
“Hmm, Spear Hero, this audience is over. Please take your leave.”
“I refuse.”
Hearing Ren’s words, Trash—perhaps feeling flustered—seems to be trying to steer things toward kicking me out. Of course, I have no intention of leaving. I know what’s coming next, after all.
“Please leave!”
The soldiers are swarming around me, trying to force me out.
“Don’t touch me, you scum.”
I’ll sweep them aside with my spear.
“Motoyasu! If you don’t cut this out—”
Just as this exchange was happening, my father—wearing only his undershirt—was dragged in by the soldiers. As I expected, staying silent only leads to this. I have to rescue him from this disgusting farce as soon as possible!
“Myne!”
Trash and Itsuki glare at my father. Ren, however, remains silent.
“W-what’s with that attitude?”
I want to rescue my Father right this very moment. But I have to time it just right.
“…I haven’t finished talking with Motoyasu-san yet, but I suppose I have no choice. Do you really have no idea what you’re accused of?”
“What do you mean, ‘no idea’… Wait, ah!”
My Father pointed at Itsuki. His intuition really is sharp. No matter how many times I see this scene, it feels like my heart is about to break.
Those soldiers always get in the way. If they don’t cut it out, I’ll kill them—just like Smoked Meat!
“So you were the one stealing from the pillow!”
“Who’s stealing from the pillow?! Naofumi-san. I never would’ve thought you were such a scoundrel!”
“Scoundrel? What are you talking about?”
“You’re in the way.”
When I swept the soldiers aside, Ren and Itsuki turned toward me for just a moment. However, my Father seems to have gone completely blank—he doesn’t even seem to notice.
“So, what are the charges against the Shield Hero?”
Perhaps realizing I’m trying to take my Father’s side, the soldiers—even after being swept aside—immediately get back up and get in the way again. Do they realize I’m holding back?
“Charges? What are you talking about?”
“Bubub… Bub… Bubububububu!”
“Huh?”
“Bububububububububu!”
Well, no matter how much you lot plan to send my Father to hell, I, Motoyasu, will stop you.
I know. I know just how kind my real Father truly is.
I know. I know that even when he goes through painful experiences, his kindness never wavers.
I know. I know he possesses a heart as vast as the ocean—a heart that, even though I unwittingly framed him, impeached him, and drove him to the brink, still accepted me despite his words of refusal.
Yes, I must repay him. No matter how many times this loop repeats, it is my mission to repay the kindness my Father has shown me.
“Bubububububububub!”
“Huh?”
“What are you talking about? After we finished eating yesterday, I was just sleeping in my room.”
“That’s a lie! Then why is Myne crying so much?!”
Isn’t that obvious? It’s because you only think about yourself.
“You’re a pig, after all. She’s probably just faking those tears.”
“Please just shut up!”
Hmm, she got mad at me. I can’t even hear a word Itsuki is saying. Compared to Father’s anger, Itsuki’s indignation is nothing but trash.
“Why are you defending Myne? And where did you even get that chainmail?”
“Ah, yesterday, while we were all drinking together, Myne dropped by the tavern. After we’d been drinking together for a while, she gave me this chainmail as a present. And… this chainmail was actually from the castle.”
“No way…”
My Father seems at a loss for words. It’s true that if someone were to say it’s the same item, I suppose it might be possible.
“That’s it! Your Majesty! I was robbed in my sleep—all my possessions and every piece of equipment except my shield were stolen! Please, catch the culprit!”
“Shut up, you scoundrel! Forcing sexual acts on my unwilling subjects is an unforgivable atrocity—if you weren’t a hero, you’d be executed on the spot!”
“……”
Ren closed his eyes as if he’d realized something.
“That’s why I’ve been saying it’s a misunderstanding! I didn’t do it!”
And then… Father’s expression turned to rage.
“You! Don’t tell me you framed me for a crime I didn’t commit just to get your hands on my dowry and equipment!”
“Ha! What are you talking about, you sex offender?”
“Don’t mess with me! You were after my money from the start, weren’t you? You planned this to distribute the equipment among your companions!”
Well, I suppose it’s about time. It gives me an unpleasant feeling, as if I’d been waiting for my Father to be framed, but I’ll save him now. I put all my strength into the spears I held in both hands.
“…This just looks like a farce.”
The moment Ren muttered that, I swept aside the soldiers who were getting in my way.
“Get out of the way! Brionac!”
Turning him into a pile of charcoal right here would leave a bad impression, so I guess I have no choice. Just this once, I’ll go easy on him as a special favor.
“‘Gwaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!’”
After sweeping them aside, I shoved the soldier holding my Father away with the shaft of my spear.
“…Huh?”
“I believe in my Father. He didn’t do it. This is a conspiracy.”
Spinning my spear in a circle, I aimed it at Trash and Itsuki.
“I suppose you’re taking advantage of the queen’s absence to do as you please, but looking at the state of this country right now, what do you think the queen would say?”
“You… Trash!”
Trash, furious that his conspiracy had been thwarted, glared at me. Immediately afterward, a voice asking a question rang in my ears.
“…The queen?”
I turned around to see Ren. Hmm, for some reason—I don’t know why—Ren seems to be listening to what I’m saying this time. Maybe I can convince him. But right now, saving my Father is the priority.
“This is the second time you’ve stepped in to protect my Father here. So, let’s use the same words…”
My Father looks up, clearly taken aback.
“I’ve come from the future to repay you for your kindness, Father.”

title: Avoiding War

That Trash and that Crimson Swine glaring at me and my Father, along with Itsuki and the soldiers of the nation. Well… what should we do? They may be the insolent fools trying to set a trap for my Father, but if we act rashly, it could lead to war. Then we’d be right back where we started.
“Father, please don’t despair. You are not alone. Even if the whole world turns against you, I, Motoyasu, will stand by your side.”
“K-Kitamura-kun…?”
I help my father to his feet, then glare at the Trash.
“How ridiculous.”
Just then, Ren calmly—and seemingly disinterested—begins to walk away from the throne room.
“Ren-san! What do you mean by that?”
“I just thought Motoyasu had a point… Even if she’s a princess, there’s a limit to punishing Naofumi based on the testimony of a single woman. Watching yesterday’s exchange, it looked like the people in the castle were just going through the motions of something that had already been decided from the start.”
My Father stared blankly at Ren and me.
“Don’t get me wrong. I’m not saying Naofumi is right. Still, it’s a fact that the Shield Hero is weak, and when Motoyasu tries to be kind to Naofumi only to be cut off every time, it’s natural to start having doubts.”
“Grr…”
“Boo-boo! Boo-boo-boo-boo-boo!”
The Crimson Swine points at my Father while squealing something. Then, it seemed to be pleading with Itsuki and Ren. Itsuki looked at his Father, his anger plain to see, while Ren simply stared impassively.
“I didn’t do it!”
“…Either way, we don’t have enough evidence to punish Naofumi. If you want to make a scene, go ahead and do it on your own. It’s a waste of time. Don’t call us over for such trivial matters.”
Looking displeased, Ren walked away. His companions followed after him.
“Bububububu!”
The Crimson Swine is squealing, isn’t it? Is it losing its temper because things aren’t going its way? I suppose it’s revealed its true form. What an ugly, truly hideous sight. I can’t let my Father look at such a vulgar creature for much longer.
“Come, Father, let’s get out of here. It’s pointless to say anything here.”
Taking Father’s hand, we leave the throne room.
“Ah… yeah.”
Ren, who had been half-convinced and half-skeptical throughout the exchange, seems to have vaguely sensed which side is at fault. It’s a positive sign, but I also sense a bit of danger. The fact remains that if we don’t move cautiously, Ren could very well be assassinated. Well, knowing Ren as I do… let’s just assume there won’t be any problems yet.
---
On our way out of the castle, the soldiers glared at us with displeasure, but when I glared back, they quickly looked away.
“Um… thanks for saving me, Kitamura… I mean, Motoyasu Kitamura.”
“It’s no big deal. I just trust my Father.”
“Yeah… I didn’t do it. I didn’t drink any sake yesterday; I was just resting at the inn.”
I talk with my father, who’s wearing just his undershirt, in the town square. This has happened before, hasn’t it? Was I actually able to save my father? I can’t help but worry that by taking his side, I might actually be putting his life in even greater danger.
“Motoyasu-kun?”
“I’d like to talk to you somewhere private for a moment.”
“Huh? Uh… sure. It’s fine—I can’t fight on my own anyway.”
“That’s true. And while we’re at it… we should get some clothes. I know you’re not alone, after all.”
To make him look as weak as possible, it might be best to have Father wear clothes that look cheap.
“Where are we going?”
“You can’t go out in just your undershirt. We’re going to buy some gear right now. Don’t worry—I’ll cover the cost.”
“I’ve got money, so it’s fine!”
Huh? Unlike the time before last, does my Father actually have money this time? He reaches inside his shield and shows me a silver coin. This is… I’m pretty sure he threw a silver coin at me back in the first world. That’s the same coin. I take my hat off to my Father’s foresight—he’s really covering all his bases.
“Motoyasu-kun. W-why are you crying?”
“There are all sorts of reasons, you know. Come on, let’s go! We’re going to buy armor for Father.”
“U-uh-huh.”
And so, I stopped by the weapons shop—which had opened early that morning—that Father apparently frequented.
The exchange after we entered the shop wasn’t much different from the one two episodes ago. The shopkeeper approached Father and, based on his character, decided to trust him.
“So? What are you going to wear, An-chan?”
“Before that, I’d like to talk to my Father—even if it’s just in the back of the shop.”
“Hm? Well, all right…”
The shopkeeper kindly led us to the back of the shop. Then, he set up a chair for us in the back room.
“Come out front once you’re done talking.”
The shopkeeper thoughtfully excused himself and left.
“What’s the matter, Motoyasu-kun?”
“First, I’d like to explain the situation to you—how to enhance our weapons and our plan moving forward.”
“Huh? Ah… yeah.”
My Father nodded, looking completely bewildered.
“First, I need to discuss something important with you.”
“What? The story about looping back from the future… I find that hard to believe on the spot.”
“It’s the truth, you know.”
“Then! Why didn’t you tell me I’d be framed for a crime I didn’t commit!?”
My Father came at me, practically shouting. I… took the full brunt of his anger.
“Well… I’m sorry. In the last loop, I told you right after I was summoned. I told you that I’d set a trap for you and drive you out penniless… and then, regarding the country’s situation… I explained that the Shield Hero is a hero worshipped in a nation hostile to this country, Melromarc.”
“Huh?”
My father stood there, completely dumbfounded. Come to think of it, that’s true. At this point, he doesn’t know that Melromarc is a human nation that discriminates against Demi-Humans. And there’s no way he could have known that the Demi-Humans worship the Shield Hero, either.
“Why didn’t you tell me!”
“There’s more to this story… On the very night you made such a fuss… I was ambushed at the castle, and Father was tricked into getting into a carriage and taken away.”
“……”
“When I finally managed to catch up, Father was on the verge of being killed by Melromarc’s soldiers. That’s what happened on the very first day after I was summoned.”
“The first day… Hmm, now that I think about it, Motoyasu-kun has been looking out for me from the very beginning. Even when I couldn’t make any friends, he tried to push his own companions onto me… He tried to teach me how to enhance my weapons and how to get stronger, too. So there was a reason he looked so uncomfortable when that woman was talking to me so familiarly.”
Just as I expected from my Father. You figured out everything from just what I said. Still, “women,” huh?
“Those are pigs.”
“Pigs…?”
“Pigs are pigs. They’re despicable lifeforms who put themselves first, think only of using others, and discard them like trash once they’re done.”
“Ah… yeah. I kind of get why Motoyasu-kun calls women pigs now. So?”
“Starting the very next day, assassins began coming for you regularly, Father, and we accepted the invitation from the envoys of Siltvelt—a nation of Demi-Humans who worship you—and set out.”
I went on to explain the events of our previous journey to my father in detail. How we crossed the border fortress, how we defeated the assassins, and how the town we stopped at was attacked. It was a short journey, but a lot happened.
“So…? What did I do once I arrived in the kingdom of Siltvelt? Did I try to take revenge on that country or something?”
“My Father didn’t do anything like that. He let it go, saying there were people who believed in him.”
“…That’s amazing. Well, I’m feeling pretty much the same way right now… If anything, I’d rather have nothing to do with those guys at all.”
“The first time the loop happened, I protected my Father just like this. Back then, to ensure Father’s happiness, I entrusted him to the envoy from Siltvelt…”
I explained the circumstances—that he had likely been killed at the border of Melromarc. Since I’d already provided context based on what happened when I went to Siltvelt earlier, Father seemed to accept it without hesitation.
“Well, that makes sense. It’s a very inconvenient situation… So last time, you broke through there and went to the country of Siltvelt, right?”
“That’s correct.”
“Then why didn’t you tell me almost anything this time… or rather, why did you only tell me weird stories?”
“What do you mean by ‘weird stories’?”
“Like my future wife being a man, or having a bird’s child.”
“Well… those are events that happened before I entered the loop.”
“What do you mean?”
I bow my head deeply. Yes, no matter how much I apologize, the sins I’ve committed will never be erased.
“Motoyasu-kun?”
“When Father was falsely accused, the place where Itsuki stood—the one that blamed you alongside the Crimson Swine—was actually me.”
“Eh…?”
“After that, my father was driven out, penniless and with no one on his side. Through steady, painstaking effort, he accomplished the great feat of proving his innocence and succeeded in destroying Trash and this country’s religion.”
“You’re jumping all over the place! I can’t find any part where you’re actually telling a strange story!”

Specifically, when modifying the bio-plants, we’ll minimize the risk of mutation as much as possible and improve them for maximum productivity. “Booh…”

“But there’s a limit to just selling food door-to-door, so we’ll eventually start selling the seeds themselves. By then, they’ll trust us, so I think they’ll manage them properly. But you never know what people will do, and we can’t trust anyone who’d let the seeds we give them wither away.”
Come to think of it, during that incident where it was falsely claimed that Filo-tan’s Finacée had been kidnapped—while Father was being pursued—the place where I fought him… had somehow turned into a dense jungle. I heard later that he was managing seeds from plants he’d modified. The plants back then were probably modified to some extent by Father so they wouldn’t wither.
However, the seeds Father is distributing to the people this time will produce plants of inferior quality. If they’re neglected, they’ll wither… By creating plants that are just a bit tougher than usual, he’s testing the people. To see if they’re managing them properly and seriously.
Those who let them wither are irresponsible and, when in trouble, commit foolish acts like invading other territories. If they manage them seriously, no problems will arise. It seems that my Father has thought this through to ensure a smooth cycle. However, simply giving them away isn’t enough.
Come to think of it, I remember that my Father was also conscious of soil management back in the village. He used to give all sorts of instructions to the monsters tasked with tending the fields. In the end, he got playfully tackled by one of the soil-tending monsters and ended up half-buried in the field; he had to be rescued by Big Sister and the village slaves.
“Things were going well for a while… but… I’d be in trouble if people started saying, ‘It’s all the Shield Hero’s fault that this village was destroyed!’ So I have to be careful about when I distribute them.”
My Father proceeds to modify the Bio-Plant seeds.
“I’ll have to make sure he takes responsibility for any Bio-Plants that wither. Even if I make them sturdy enough not to wither… if they aren’t properly tended, they might still die, and ultimately, the plants might be driven from their homes. It’d be a disaster if this place turned into a ‘Land of Death,’ wouldn’t it?”
That’s a bit of a hard pill to swallow. Given the bio-plants’ mutability, there’s no doubt the seeds I handed out put the village to the southwest in a difficult situation. If that happens, the trust placed in me as a saint could easily turn against me.
I suppose that’s what Father is worried about. That’s why I have to exercise the utmost caution when handing them out—and sell the seeds instead.
“All right, now that I’ve finished modifying the plants to produce sturdy fruits for peddling, I think I’ll ask Elena to lend me some of her land.”
“Booh…”
“Yeah, if things go well, I’ll be able to make some money, too.”
And so, my immediate sales plan proceeded steadily forward.

Because of that trauma, I couldn’t rest easy until I’d seen Filolial-sama grow up and become an angel with my own eyes.

These were the events leading up to the wave.

Also, Takt might be in Faubrey, but I don’t think you need to be too wary of him. After all, by then, Ren, Itsuki, and I will be right by Motoyasu-kun’s side.”
“But Takt’s remaining followers will cause trouble.”
“We’ll rely on the King of Faubrey for that. And as for Takt’s… well, his entourage is full of beautiful women, so if we handle it skillfully, we can avoid a war. No doubt about it.”
“Is that so?”
“Yeah, the King of Faubrey wants the Four Saints more than the Seven Stars, but he’s the kind of person who knows how to hold back. So even a pretty unreasonable request should go through.”
“I see.”
“Well, it doesn’t have to be Faubrey—any other country would work, too. If we take Melty-chan’s advice, I think we’d be more likely to run into them there.”
I see. Motoyasu, I’ve taken Father’s wish to heart.
“One last thing… Motoyasu, I was so happy to have your help. I can’t thank you enough. I know it might be selfish of me to ask this after everything, but could I ask you for a favor?”
“Just tell me what you need.”
There’s no doubt in Father’s words. Above all, if he’s asking me for a favor, I simply can’t refuse.
“Right now… I think Ren and Itsuki are filled with regret.”
“They’re undoubtedly regretting it.”
I picture Ren and Itsuki, whose whereabouts are currently unknown. Since the loop hasn’t restarted, they must still be alive somewhere. They’re probably pale-faced and in despair.
“Even though we tried to stop them time and time again, they went through with it anyway. I think it’s their own fault.”
“That’s true.”
“But I want you to help them.”
…Help Ren and Itsuki? Considering this loop, I don’t see any need for it at all…
“I’m sure right now, they regret it so much they’d want to kill themselves. If they could go back to that day, I think they’d say they want to act differently so this wouldn’t happen.”
That day, you say? You must be referring to the very first day we arrived in this world. I’m about to loop back to that day myself. Which means, Father…
“Of course, it’s not just for emotional reasons. If we can win Ren and Itsuki over and put our enhancement methods into practice, there won’t be any allies more reliable than them.”
It’s true—if we can make that happen, both Ren and Itsuki will be incredibly strong. In fact, in the first world, they were just as strong as I am.
“So… just as you helped me, I want you to help Ren and Itsuki.”
To ask me to help Ren and Itsuki—the very ones who turned the world into this mess. You really are kind, Father. If the Father from the first world heard that, he’d probably just snort in derision. But I respect both this version of you and the one from before. …In that case, there’s only one thing I can say.
“Understood. I, Motoyasu, will save Ren and Itsuki.”
“Yeah, thanks. Sorry for always asking you to do the impossible…”
Hearing my words, my Father gave me a smile.
“Motoyasu, I can only offer the usual platitudes, but do your best… Even if everything ends up being erased, I’m rooting for you.”
“Yes, sir.”
When my Father waved, everyone waved back.
“Well then, see you later—”
I selected the “No” option. Then, just like when the loop began, my vision froze, a clock appeared, and the spear began to vibrate and spin backward. It seems there are multiple conditions required to trigger a loop using the Minute Hand of the Dragon Hourglass.
Since I’ve defeated the Four Spirits by this point, I probably won’t fail, but considering the process, it’s also true that it would take too long. In that case, let’s try acting according to what my Father said.
If I do too many good deeds, civil unrest will break out, and Itsuki will come to view us as enemies. As a result, it will trigger the Four Spirits’ rampage.
To fulfill Father’s wish, I’ll return once more to that moment in time. As I’ve thought before, I’ll keep my promise to Father based on the information I’ve gained from the loop.
And so, I—returned to the past once again.
-----
The Melromarc arc has come to an end. Starting with the next episode, we’ll move on to the Faubrey arc.
